'''Carldell "Squeaky" Johnson''' (born January 28, 1983) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UAB Blazers men's basketball|UAB Blazers]] from 2003 to 2006 after beginning his collegiate career at [[Salt Lake Community College]]. Since turning professional in 2006, he has spent time with three different teams in [[Mexico]] and two in Belgium, as well as having multiple stints with the [[Austin Spurs]] (then Austin Toros) of the [[NBA Development League]]. He has been a non-roster invitee of the [[San Antonio Spurs]] on two occasions and played with the [[New Orleans Hornets]] during the [[2011–12 NBA season]].

Johnson holds the record for the most games played for the Austin Toros/Austin Spurs, having a total of 230 games played with the organization.

==Early years==
Johnson was born on January 28, 1983, in [[New Orleans]], [[Louisiana]], to Lonnie Johnson and Elise Ramsey. He has one brother.<ref name="UAB">{{cite web|title=Player Bio: Carldell Johnson|url=http://www.uabsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/johnson_carldell00.html|work=UABSports.com|accessdate=December 27, 2011|archive-date=April 19, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120419010424/http://www.uabsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/johnson_carldell00.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> When he was 17 years old, his father died of [[cancer]]. In December 2011, Carldell said that, "My whole life, I’ve been trying to grind it out and work hard to get where I need to be. My father died from cancer, and I grew up in a tough neighborhood in (eastern) New Orleans, where guys would get bored and find time to get into other things, like stealing cars and walking around looking for fights. But Coach Tillman would always pick me up and have us going to practice, whether it was basketball season or not."<ref name=NOLA>{{cite news|last=Reid|first=John|title=Guard Carldell 'Squeaky' Johnson hoping his long journey ends at home with the New Orleans Hornets|url=http://www.nola.com/hornets/index.ssf/2011/12/squeaky_hoping_his_long_journe.html|accessdate=December 27, 2011|work=NOLA.com|date=December 21, 2011}}</ref>  He attended [[John F. Kennedy High School (New Orleans)|John F. Kennedy High School]] in New Orleans and transferred to [[Marion Abramson High School]] for his senior year.<ref name=NOLA/> At Abramson he played basketball under head coach Robert Tillman. Tillman was also Johnson's coach in [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] basketball.<ref name="NOLA"/> After high school, he was not recruited by any division one schools to play basketball, so he attended [[Salt Lake Community College]], where he was the team's starting [[point guard]]. He averaged eight points and eight [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] during his one season there.<ref name="UAB"/> Following the season, Tillman approached then-[[University of Alabama-Birmingham]] head basketball coach [[Mike Anderson (basketball, born 1959)|Mike Anderson]] and told him to, "just watch [Johnson] a little bit; get all your players together and play a pickup game and let him guard your point guard." Eventually, as Tillman says in an interview with ''[[The Times-Picayune]]'', "They went out there and played, and after it was all over, Mike said he was going to give him a try, but he would have to sit out his first year."<ref name="NOLA"/>

During [[Hurricane Katrina]] in 2006, his mother Elise had her house in New Orleans destroyed, but managed to evacuate to [[Houston, Texas]], before joining Carldell in [[Birmingham, Alabama]]. Presently, she resides in Houston.<ref name="NOLA"/>

==College career==
In his first season playing for the [[UAB Blazers]], Johnson started in 22 of 32 games and led the nation in assist–to–turnover ratio, averaging 3.83 assists for every turnover he committed. He finished the season averaging 4.8 points, 1.8 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], and a team-leading 4.3 assists per game.<ref name=BBB>{{cite web|title=Player Profile: Carldell Johnson |url=http://basketballbeyondborders.com/Players%20Profile%20%20pages/Player_Profile_Carldell%20Johnson.htm |work=Basketball Beyond Borders |accessdate=December 27, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120426073148/http://basketballbeyondborders.com/Players%20Profile%20%20pages/Player_Profile_Carldell%20Johnson.htm |archive-date=April 26, 2012 }}</ref> Johnson also finished the season with a total of 137 assists and 71 [[Steal (basketball)|steal]]s. On March 12, 2004, he achieved his first career [[double-double]], recording 14 points and 11 assists against the [[DePaul Blue Demons]]. In his junior season, he played in all 33 of UAB's games, starting 32 of them. For the second straight season, he led the conference in assists-to-turnover ratio. Johnson recorded a season-high of nine assists on two occasions, first against [[Louisville Cardinals|Louisville]] and then against DePaul. In the DePaul game, he played in a career-high 41 minutes. At season's end, he was named as a nominee for the [[Bob Cousy Award]], given to the nation's top point guard.<ref name=UAB /> In his senior season at UAB, he finished with averages of 7.3 points, 3.0 rebounds, 6.3 assists, and 2.6 steals per game.<ref name=BBB />

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[2006 NBA draft]], Johnson was selected in the sixth round of the 2006 [[Continental Basketball Association]] draft by the [[Vancouver Dragons]]. However, he never played for the team. He later signed with [[VOO Wolves Verviers-Pepinster|Verviers-Pepinster]] of [[Basketball League Belgium|Belgium]] for the 2006–07 season. In 32 games with the team, he averaged 4.5 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 2.7 assists per game.<ref name="BBB"/>

In August 2007, he joined [[Halcones UV Xalapa]] of [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto Profesional|Mexico]], where he played three games. In those games, he averaged 15.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 5.0 assists.

On November 1, 2007, he was selected in the second round of the [[2007 NBA Development League draft]] by the [[Austin Toros]].<ref>{{cite web|title=D-League Draft 2007|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/dleague_draft_07.html|work=NBA.com|accessdate=December 27, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081220032931/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/dleague_draft_07.html|archive-date=2008-12-20|url-status=dead}}</ref> Johnson played 49 games for the Toros in the 2007–08 season, averaging 4.1 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 3.6 assists per game.

In August 2008, he joined Halcones UV Córdoba of Mexico but left before appearing in a game for them. In October 2008, he was re-acquired by the Austin Toros. On January 29, 2009, he was waived by the Toros due to injury. After his release, he once again returned to Mexico, signing with the [[Bravos de Piedras Negras]]. He played in four games for the team and finished with averages of 10.5 points, 1.8 rebounds, 5.3 assists, and 3.0 steals per game. On February 15, 2009, he was re-acquired by the Toros.<ref name="realgm">{{cite web|title=Carldell Johnson Player Profile|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Squeaky_Johnson/Summary/1760|publisher=[[RealGM]]|accessdate=December 27, 2011}}</ref> He played 47 games in the 2008–09 season and averaged 8.7 points, 3.1 rebounds, and 5.1 assists per game.<ref name="BBB"/>

In July 2009, Johnson joined the [[San Antonio Spurs]] for the 2009 [[NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Guilleminault|first=Eric|title=2009 NBA Summer League Rosters|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/node/8843|work=NBADraft.net|accessdate=December 27, 2011|date=July 5, 2009|archive-date=March 9, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120309055840/http://www.nbadraft.net/node/8843|url-status=dead}}</ref> In November 2009, he was re-acquired by the Austin Toros. He went on to play in 56 games and averaged 7.0 points, 1.8 rebounds, and 2.9 assists per game.<ref name="BBB"/>

In July 2010, he re-joined the San Antonio Spurs for the 2010 NBA Summer League.<ref>{{cite news|last=Guilleminault|first=Eric|title=2010 NBA Las Vegas Summer League Game Schedule & Rosters|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/2010-nba-las-vegas-summer-league-game-schedule-rosters|accessdate=December 27, 2011|work=NBADraft.net|date=June 26, 2010}}</ref> In October 2010, he was again re-acquired by the Toros. He played in 46 games for the team that season and finished with averages of 12.3 points, 4.0 rebounds, 6.0 assists, and 1.5 steals per game.<ref name="BBB"/>

In November 2011, Johnson was again re-acquired by the Toros. On December 9, 2011, he signed with the New Orleans Hornets.<ref>{{cite news|title=HORNETS ADD NINE PLAYERS|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/hornets_add_nine_players_2011_12_09.html|accessdate=December 27, 2011|work=NBA.com|date=December 9, 2011}}</ref> He would make his NBA debut around that time. On February 7, 2012, he was waived by the Hornets.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/hornets_request_waivers_on_joh_2012_02_08.html HORNETS REQUEST WAIVERS ON JOHNSON AND SUMMERS]</ref> On February 10, 2012, he returned to the Toros.

In September 2012, Johnson signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11006 |title=Hawks add James Anderson, Keith Benson, Damion James, Carldell Johnson, Anthony Tolliver to training camp |access-date=2012-09-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130206091240/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11006 |archive-date=2013-02-06 |url-status=dead }}</ref> However, he was later by the Hawks on October 17, 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11188 |title=Hawks waive guard Carldell Johnson |access-date=2012-10-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221095537/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11188 |archive-date=2014-02-21 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On February 11, 2014, Johnson was re-acquired by the Austin Toros.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/cardell_johnson_returns__aus_2014_02_11.html |title=Cardell 'Squeaky' Johnson Returns To Austin Toros |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2014-02-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222100454/http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/cardell_johnson_returns__aus_2014_02_11.html |archive-date=2014-02-22 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On March 15, 2014, he had his highest scoring game of the season, scoring 20 in a loss to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Austin Toros Fall To Rio Grande Valley Vipers 128-115|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4752076|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=March 15, 2014|accessdate=March 15, 2014}}</ref>

On October 6, 2014, Johnson signed with [[Toros de Aragua]] of the [[Liga Profesional de Baloncesto]].<ref>[http://www.liderendeportes.com/noticias/baloncesto/exnba-carldell-johnson-es-tercer-foraneo-de-toros.aspx Exnba Carldell Johnson es tercer foráneo de Toros] {{in lang|es}}</ref>

In November 2014, Johnson signed with Valvoline of Mongolia for the 2014–15 season, making history by becoming the first American basketball player to compete in Mongolia.<ref>{{cite web |title=American professional basketball player to compete in Mongolian Super League 2014-2015 |url=http://www.infomongolia.com/ct/ci/8624 |date=November 19, 2014 |accessdate=November 20, 2014 |work=InfoMongolia.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141123050723/http://www.infomongolia.com/ct/ci/8624 |archive-date=November 23, 2014 }}</ref>

In March 2016, Johnson joined the [[Náuticos de Mazatlán]] of the Mexican [[Circuito de Baloncesto de la Costa del Pacífico]] (CIBACOPA) ahead of the 2016 season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://cibacopa.org/noticias/llega-nba-al-navio/|title=Llega NBA al navío|publisher=[[CIBACOPA]]|date=March 18, 2016|access-date=July 6, 2023|language=es|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230130172423/https://cibacopa.org/noticias/llega-nba-al-navio/|archive-date=January 30, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> He was loaned to the [[Frayles de Guasave]] the following month.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.debate.com.mx/guasave/Frayles-visita-a-Caballeros-con-caras-nuevas-en-roster-20160419-0061.html|title=Frayles visita a Caballeros con caras nuevas en róster|work=Debate.com.mx|first=Edgar|last=Vega|date=April 19, 2016|access-date=5 July 2023|language=es|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422163105/http://www.debate.com.mx/guasave/Frayles-visita-a-Caballeros-con-caras-nuevas-en-roster-20160419-0061.html|archive-date=April 22, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
For the 2019–20 season, Johnson was added to the coaching staff of the G League's [[Memphis Hustle]] as an assistant.<ref>{{cite news|url= http://www.desototimes.com/sports/hustle-coaching-staff-set-for-season/article_f5d349aa-f4f8-11e9-83cf-6b9f83ddc958.html |title= Hustle coaching staff set for season |date = October 22, 2019 |publisher= desototimes.com|accessdate=November 17, 2019}}</ref>
